title: Add RAG agent templates, tool-calling examples, and docs quickstarts
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Add a set of reusable RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent templates and companion tool-calling examples to make it easy for engineers to bootstrap document-aware agents. This PR introduces canonical templates, example tool adapters (search, vector DB lookup, and external API callers), and three quickstart pages in the docs site with runnable snippets and a reference playbook. Changes are docs-first and example-focused to reduce friction when teams adopt RAG patterns on Redwood. Checklist: - [x] Add RAG agent templates (chat + action loop) - [x] Add tool-calling examples (search, embeddings lookup, external API) - [x] Add quickstart docs with copy/paste examples and SDK snippets (TS/Python) - [x] Add unit E2E sample tests for examples folder - [x] Update docs site navigation and TOC - [x] Add CI linting for new files Notes: The docs content is intentionally descriptive with guidance for prompt design, caching, and fallbacks for private deployments. Examples include both simple and production-minded variants (prefix caching, soft-fallback to smaller models). This is a docs and examples-only change; there are no runtime code modifications to the serving layer. Related work: Linear ENG-9123, DOC-411. For reviewers: focus on clarity of the quickstarts, whether example tool adapters are idiomatic for SDKs, and whether the README examples match the new docs snippets.
